Figure 2

Money and taxes are where chatbots most often stand in for paid help

We asked 1,850 current chatbot users which of ten parts of their lives they use their main chatbot for, and then, for each one, what they now do less of. The answers sort into inputs people used to pay for (a professional, an app or service) and inputs that were free (asking others, free tutorials, working it out alone).

Share of each domain's users who say they now do less of each input

Hover a row to read its values. Click to keep it highlighted.

Sort rows by

Each row is one domain, and respondents could choose several inputs, so row totals can exceed 100%. The column on the right counts anyone who chose at least one paid input. Prolific US sample, fielded Aug 22–25, 2026, after quality screens.

Source: authors' survey of US chatbot users, fielded August 22–25, 2026 (n = 1,850 after quality screens).

Finances, budgeting and taxes ranks first on the paid-input measure: 47% of its users say they cut back on a professional, a paid product, or both. Government and legal tasks and mental health come next, both driven by fewer visits to professionals. For shopping, hobbies and household chores, the chatbot mostly replaces free search and the user's own effort.

The finance row also has the highest share cutting a paid product (34%). Paid tax software faces the same substitution pressure as professional help.
